description: Vectors of the rules of the per-scale volumes: the design limits, one invalid vector per rule on the sample figure (a rule must report it, at the scale it names, and a measured value must move the wrong way against the baseline), the scales on which the unpatched sample passes each rule, and hand-computed meshes for the geometry that the owned checks and the oracle (shapely, trimesh) both measure.

excavator.description: A 12 m long bar of 0.4 m cross section seen against a copy shortened by 5 mm: the band is not collapsed to the voxel count of the fine body.

viewsPosition.description: `volumes-views-disagree` compares the place as well as the extent of the whole asset along a shared axis. The side elevation of the sample at 1:100 covers -0.1596 to 0.21 m along the length (0.3696 m); the plan is replaced by one filled rectangle on the root of the same length, 0.54 m wide, moved ahead by `shiftM`. The extents agree in every case (difference 0); the limit is max(15 mm, 2 % of 0.3696 m) = 15 mm, so a plan 10 mm ahead passes and one 50 mm ahead is a finding that names both intervals.

cases.name: a plan drawn 10 mm ahead of the side elevation is within one feature
a plan drawn 50 mm ahead of the side elevation has the right length in the wrong place

typified.description: Typification of a row at a coarser scale (C22 extended): 13 rods of 12 mm at 75 mm pitch (centres 0 to 0.9 m, 1 m high) are drawn at 1:500 as 4 posts of 75 mm at 0.275 m pitch (centres 0.0375 to 0.8625 m). Posts and rods disagree part by part, but the posts are `envelope` solids on the bone of the row, so cross-scale compares the convex hull of the posts (0 to 0.9 m, area 0.9 m²) with the convex hull of the rods (-0.006 to 0.906 m, area 0.912 m²): IoU 0.9 / 0.912 = 0.986842. Without the declaration the posts stay posts and fail against the hull.

outlines.name: an unfilled closed outline around a part the 3D fills counts as filled in every boundary measure

envelopeArea.pocket: the areas of the other regions stay equal up to `pocketFraction` of their value: with the arms as walls one face sample of the legs under the torso looks, beyond the torso, into the armpit, a pocket of 19 mm that the flood of 1:200 (cell 7.5 mm) does not reach, so the torso does not stand between that sample and the air; without the arms the pocket is open
envelopeArea.name: the arms of the sample modelled as porous envelope prisms

retained.description: Per view three cuboids along the cut axis (wholly on the low side, wholly on the high side, crossing the plane at 0) with projected footprints 1, 2 and 3 m2: the area of the projection of the retained half, far (default) and near, by hand.

stroke.description: Slender cuboids drawn as strokes (C24): a bar of 1 m x 10 mm and a copy 2 m beside it, pen 50 mm; and a bar of 1 m x 80 mm (wider than the pen) keeps its true width. Stroke area = (length + width) x width.

cases.name: thin
wide

mechanical.description: Undoes what makes the sample figure a valid asset (a 1 mm shift of the head per scale and shoes at 1:500) so that it is again the mechanical copy that the copied and bones rules must flag.

burial.description: A laptop base 0.4 x 0.02 x 0.3 m standing on a table top 2 x 0.05 x 1 m: the top face of the table is two triangles of 1 m2, of which the laptop buries its footprint of 0.12 m2 only; the exposed area of the table is its surface 2 x (2 x 0.05 + 2 x 1 + 0.05 x 1) = 4.3 m2 minus 0.12 m2.

outer.description: C29: the outer area of the union of the solids of one region, faces buried by the same region left out. A unit cube and a cube of 0.5 sticking out of its +x face by 0.25: the unit cube loses 0.25 of one face, the small cube shows 0.25 + 4 x 0.125; total 6.5.

porous.description: C26: the torso and the arms of the sample declared as exchange regions; their 2D shapes are bound to them, so their outlines are soft in the silhouette and their solids are a soft band in the cross-scale volume.

hollow.description: C30: a cup modelled as a hollow revolve with a wall of 0.2 mm, 100 mm long and 80 mm across: volumes-feature judges its overall extents (80 mm), not its wall.

tangent.description: A roof of 2 m x 1.004 m and a bar of 1 m x 0.5 m above it tessellated inside its outline, in one elevation with a raster cell of 10 mm: the hairline between them lies under the centre of one row of cells. Gaps of 2 mm (a fifth of a cell) are closed, a gap of 3 mm (0.3 cell) is real and stays; the closing of shapely with the radius of an eighth of a cell is the oracle.

cases.name: gap of 2 mm
gap of 3 mm

bodyEdge.description: An unfilled closed outline that is the edge of a body (the solids as they are fill at least half of what it encloses): its centre line is the body edge and the pen is drawing convention, so a slender solid along it keeps its true width. A plate of 1 m x 0.6 m with a rim wire of 10 mm along its upper edge (centre line on the edge), outlined by a closed stroke of 80 mm pen on the bone of both: the reference is the plate and the wire at 10 mm, 0.6 + 1.01 x 0.005 + 2 x 0.005 x 0.005 = 0.6051 m² (at the pen it would be 0.6 + 1.08 x 0.04 + 2 x 0.04 x 0.04 = 0.6464 m², 0.04 m fatter than the drawing all along the edge); the drawing counts as filled up to the centre line, 0.6 m², IoU 0.6 / 0.6051 = 0.9916. The same outline around the wire alone encloses a void: the wire is drawn at the pen, (1 + 0.08) x 0.08 = 0.0864 m².

follow.description: C24 refined: a slender solid is drawn like the 2D shape it follows. A bar of 1 m x 10 mm on bone b along x; the drawn shapes of the viewpoint are given by bone, closedness, fill, rings and pen; the stroke area is (length + width) x width. A hoop (a revolve loop of a 16-gon tube of 10 mm radius, 0.5 m from the axis) is slender by the path it follows and is drawn as an annulus.
